criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-gate`. A hand-built squash that adds the records of two or more jobs linked by previous_job and base_fingerprint, with the last job's fingerprint equal to the squashed tree, passes both invariant::check and jobs::check.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-gate`. Tests show each of these is refused with the message in design §4.3: a /1 candidate in a chain, no head or a wrong head base, a fork, an unlinked or missing middle job, a broken fingerprint link, a last job that does not match the tree, a chain that changes a .gitattributes file.
criteria.evidence: These tests passed, and each asserts the §4.3 wording: a_candidate_1_in_a_chain_is_refused, a_chain_without_a_head_or_with_a_wrong_head_is_refused, a_forked_chain_is_refused, an_unlinked_or_missing_middle_job_is_refused, a_broken_fingerprint_link_is_refused, a_last_job_that_does_not_match_the_tree_is_refused, a_chain_that_changes_a_classification_rules_file_is_refused. Messages for cases §4.3 does not cover (two heads, a .gitattributes in the diff) are recorded in the design's progress note.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-gate`. A chain on a commit with two parents is refused. A partly landed chain is judged correctly: one job left uses the single-job rule, and two or more left with a landed predecessor, including a /1 predecessor, are accepted.
criteria.evidence: a_chain_on_a_commit_with_two_parents_is_refused passed. It checks that landing_job is empty and asserts the merge message that check actually shows (§4.6). a_partly_landed_chain_is_judged_by_the_jobs_left passed and covers one job left with a stale base, two jobs left with a /2 predecessor, two with a /1 predecessor, and an unlanded predecessor, which is refused.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-gate`. Chains with repeated fingerprints (a job that reverts an earlier one, a job that changes no governed content) land.
criteria.evidence: chains_with_repeated_fingerprints_land passed. It covers A→B→A→C and a job whose base_fp equals its fp, and asserts that invariant, jobs and history all report no violations.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-gate`. summary: The change builds the gate half of D69, as the request and the reading ask. `landing` in invariant.rs now accepts a squash that closes several jobs when their athena.candidate/2 records form one chain. The order comes from previous_job. There must be exactly one head, and its base must be the parent's fingerprint or a predecessor already landed on the parent, including a /1 predecessor. The fingerprint links must hold, and the last job must match the tree. Every job also runs the factored-out per-job checks. A chain is refused on a commit with more than one parent and when a .gitattributes file changes. `landing_job` now returns a set, `jobs::check` accepts every job of a chain, and the history walk records every job of it. A single-job landing takes the same `job_problem` path with the landed fingerprint, so it is exactly as strict as before. I ran `cargo test -p athena-gate`: 67 tests passed, including 15 new chain tests that cover every case in §5 item 4 that belongs to the gate. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` are clean. The docs are updated (enforcement.md row M30, D69 marked accepted, v0 §7.3, CHANGELOG, records.md, architecture.md), and no governance file or records/ path changed. Two small gaps: no test covers a middle job that had already landed on the parent (only the history-walk case is tested), and the new M30 row sits out of numeric order in the table.
